NRL Casualty Ward: Fresh Reynolds injury; Ramien's season over
Broncos veteran Adam Reynolds faces a battle to return to the field before hanging up the boots after suffering a calf strain at training on Wednesday.
The premiership winner has not played since suffering a head knock in the Round 22 loss to the Knights and the latest setback puts his hopes of playing out his final season before retiring at the end of the year at risk.
In a statement, the Broncos said Reynolds will be assessed on a weekly basis to determine a return to play.
"Scans at the Clive Berghofer Centre’s Qscan facility confirmed that Broncos captain Adam Reynolds sustained a grade 1 soleus strain on his right calf at training yesterday," the club said.
"His return-to-play timeline will be determined on a week-by-week basis."
Cronulla centre Jesse Ramien has also played his final game for the club with the centre undergoing season-ending pectoral surgery on Thursday.
Ramien suffered the injury in the second half of last week's loss to St George Illawarra and will depart the Sharks at the end of the season to join the Cowboys.
"A big blow for the Sharks with Jesse Ramien ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season after undergoing pectoral repair surgery today," the club said in a statement.
"The star centre hurt himself in the second half against the Dragons on Sunday afternoon; he then went for scans on Monday, but after seeing a specialist, it was decided the best course of action was surgery."
In Friday night's clash at Accor Stadium, the Rabbitohs lost Adam Elliott to a groin injury early in the first half.
The Bunnies have lost halfback Ashton Ward (hamstring) for the remainder of the season while Jamie Humphreys is also sidelined with an ankle injury. The Rabbitohs have said he is a week-to-week proposition with a chronic ankle issue.
The Bulldogs lost winger Jethro Rinakama to a knee injury during Friday night's loss to Souths.

items.body_excerpt:
Presented By
NRL Match Preview: Round 24 v Raiders
The Sharks take on the Raiders at Ocean Protect Stadium tomorrow, aiming to bounce back from a shock loss to the Dragons.
They had more than 100 First Nations fans turn out to cheer the team on at captain’s run this morning.
The club ran the event for a third straight year, in partnership with Deadly Choices and the Central and Eastern Sydney Public Health Network to inspire the next generation for Indigenous Round.
“Very special considering the number of Indigenous representations we have in our club,” coach Craig Fitzgibbon said.
“It’s important to our Indigenous players, and they do a really great job in that space, to be honest.
“They represent it well, and it’s definitely important that we wear the jersey with a bit more Shark-like intensity tomorrow.”
Cronulla will be playing for Jesse Ramien tomorrow too, after the star centre was ruled out for the season with a pectoral injury.
The 29-year-old is moving to the Cowboys next year and was dreaming of a fairytale finish in the Shire; he’s spent the best part of a decade at the club.
“Everyone is hurting for Jesse. Obviously, he’s been a long-time Shark and a really valuable member and moving on, so losing a player like that knocks the players around,” the Sharks coach shared.
“It’s probably similar to the narrative that he’s leaving, so it probably strengthens that opportunity to show what he does mean to his teammates.”
They’ll have to do so without Addin Fonua-Blake as well, who has been suspended for a week for a high shot.
And up against a Raiders side still fuming from having their finals hopes dashed last weekend.
“They were last year’s minor premiers, so they’ve got something about them. They’ve got a lot of speed and talent in their side,” Fitzgibbon added.
“And now they’ve got nothing to lose, so they’ll be a handful, and I have a lot of respect for Ricky (Stuart).
“I had a lot of time with him as a player, and he was my coach so I know how he can motivate and inspire a side.”
Fitzgibbon was the Clive Churchill Medal winner in 2002 under Ricky Stuart at the Roosters.
Stuart would then beat Fitzgibbon in the now Sharks coach's first NRL game in charge in 2022.
After that, Fitzgibbon would lose his next two matchups against Ricky’s Raiders, before turning it around, winning 5 of their now 9 encounters.
Cronulla got the chocolates earlier this season in round 4, winning 34-22 in Canberra, and are now hoping to win a third straight game at home against them for the first time since 2002.
It’s also been over two decades since anyone has challenged Andrew Ettingshausen or David Peachey’s try-scoring records at the Sharks.
The legendary fullback now sits equal second all-time alongside Ronaldo Mulitalo, who could jump into outright second tomorrow if he crosses for a four-pointer.
Mulitalo has 110 tries in the black, white and blue, and the 26-year-old is 56 away from ET's club record.
Braydon Trindall’s already got Cronulla’s most try assists in a season record snapped up but could challenge for the NRL record with 4 more games in the regular season.
His halves partner, Nicho Hynes, has 25 assists this season as well; the pair is well out in front of any other combination in the competition in that statistic.
Hynes, fresh from equalling Nathan Cleary’s second-placed record of 32 straight conversions; he needs eight points to reach 1,100 points in the NRL and is 21 points away from passing Luke Covell (948) for the third most points for Cronulla.
The Sharks have won 6 home games in a row, making Shark Park a fortress this season, with no losses there since round 3.

Perhaps, the timely loss could do a trick a refocus this team ahead of the Finals.
A loss which sums up their season
The Raiders were upset at home 30-24 by the Knights last week, unable to take advantage of their opponents’ shortcomings and lack of quality within their team. Locked at 18-all at HT, they were overpowered in the second half by a team which showed a higher level of desire. With an equal share of possession, they completed at just 81%, ran for 9.3m per carry, and made 530 PCM’s. Attack wasn’t their issues; rather, they were let down by their defensive execution. They missed 35 tackles and allowed 10 line breaks. Offering their opponents numerous opportunities to score points was the major difference in the second half. This also demonstrated a lack of maturity in the Raiders, a factor which has plagued them throughout 2026.
Stats that matter
- These two sides met in Round 4 where the Sharks were victorious 34-22. They have an edge returning home, winning 59% of matches played here compared to the Raiders 43%.
- The Sharks have won 5 of the past 6 matches against the Raiders. In the past 5 matches, the average margin of victory has been 18 points, with 3 games decided by 14 points or more. The average total points in the same games is 48.4 points.
- The Sharks are the superior team on both sides of the ball in 2026. They score 29ppg compared to the Raiders 22ppg and concede just 20ppg, while the Raiders leak 25ppg.
A bounce back win is needed
Following a poor loss to a lowly ranked opponent, the Sharks need to make a positive statement. The ideal way to achieve that is to come out and win this game in impressive fashion. The Raiders have been competitive recently but are still missing and edge to their game which saw them capture the Minor Premiership last season. The home side has several player issues to overcome, namely the loss of AFB (suspension) and Ramien (injury). Winning 8 games from 10 matches at home this season, as well as playing during the day, should ensure the Sharks overcome the challenges which come their way.
The Raiders have struggled on the road in 2026, winning just 4 matches, and they will be further tested to match the quality and intensity of the Sharks. The loss last week for the Sharks comes at a good time; never does a team want a loss but heading into the Finals, it will refocus them and boost the determination to execute to the standard they have previously set. Bulldogs vs Rabbitohs Preview & Betting Tips: NRL Round 24 2026
August 13 th 2026, 1:24pm , By: Scooby
The second game of NRL action on Friday night will take place in Sydney as the Bulldogs host the Rabbitohs . With both teams flirting with the edge of the Top 8, this game is worth more than just the two competition points as the winner could be set on a path towards the NRL Finals. This ensures that a thrilling contest awaits, and fans will be on the edge of their seats for this match. Before You Bet is here with a detailed look at what is ahead in this contest.
Also, Before You Bet will be providing free previews and betting tips for EVERY game in the 2026 NRL season, so make sure to head over to our NRL Tips regularly to keep up to date with all of our free content.
Bulldogs vs Rabbitohs Predictions & Tips: NRL Round 24 2026
Coming up short
The Bulldogs needed a win last week against the Roosters but failed to demonstrate experience and poise when it mattered most. Trailing 8-2 at HT, they pulled their way back into the match to lead 18-8 with 15 minutes remaining. The fast finish of their opponents meant they were unable to halt their momentum, as a horror completion rate (66%), lack of power (7.8m per carry), and 31 missed tackles hurt their momentum. Despite their poor finish, they can take positives away from the match as their attack continued to improve and pressured the Roosters in areas other teams haven’t been able to achieve.
Scraping home (in style)
Up 28-nil at HT against the Eels, the Rabbitohs were flying and looked every bit a quality team that could cause headaches for other teams inside the Top 8. Unfortunately, their scoring stopped, and they came out a vastly different team in the second half, eventually prevailing 28-24. The win saw them only control 46% possession and complete at 80%, continually making mistakes in the second half to give their opponents key territory. The finish shouldn’t eliminate the positives either. Their 10.1m per carry, 11 line breaks, and just 24 missed tackles are positive points to build upon in coming weeks.
Stats that matter
- These two sides met in Round 5 where the Rabbitohs were victorious 32-24. They have a slightly better record at this ground, winning 57% of matches compared to the Bulldogs 54%.
- In the past 5 matches, 4 games have been decided by 8 points or less. The average margin is still high (10.8 points) courtesy of a blowout 32-point win. The average total points in the same games is 46.8 points.
- The Rabbitohs have the superior attacking this season compared to the Bulldogs (19ppg vs 27ppg) but the Bulldogs are stronger defensively (22pg vs 24ppg) by allowing fewer points.
A close call
There is more than just 2 competition points on the line in this game, with a spot in the Finals likely decided upon this result. The Bulldogs have an edge and are listed as favourites. Their resurgence in positive form has many overlooking their shortcomings. While good last week, they gave up a winning chance. If they can produce that same standard here, they are a strong winning hope. The Rabbitohs have numerous flaws but seem to get ‘up’ for bigger matches. Their depth will be further challenged ahead of this match as Ward is replaced by Sullivan at halfback; the return of Graham boosts their edge and their bench, as Gray moves back there.
This game will go down to the wire. The Rabbitohs can bring a defensive pressure when needed and the Bulldogs will relish this challenge. Providing they can eliminate their mistakes, the Rabbitohs are a chance of winning this contest. So too are the Bulldogs but their recent form has reduced the attention on their shortcomings. The odds should have the two teams closer than what they are but rather than chase an upset victory, play it safe and invest on this game to be a thrilling contest that is only decided in the remaining few minutes.
